title: fusion.repair-result/v1
description: Frozen at plan step 15 on Prior's answer 69 at a4f463f: the module's answer to a fusion.repair.v1 invocation, the asset Prior selects as EnvelopeSchema the way external_explorer.go at 6080ba76 selects the explorer's. The explorer envelope's two members, extended for a run of several roles. domain.status takes four values: completed, the close step wrote the record and every step before it completed; escalated, the workflow stopped for the user at a named step (a blocked implementer, a failed or oversize capture, a revise verdict past revise_bound, an escalate verdict, a correction-required integration, an audit that did not pass, a known closure precondition conflict), with what ran so far in result; refused, the invocation or an answer violated its schema or bound; recovery-required, a role stood at accepted, a required audit was missing or invalid, or an integration or closure is unknown or in flight, never a fabricated audit or a fresh inference (67.5), and never a terminal refusal written to end the run. The host stores one verified terminal envelope under the workflow owner: completed records a successful operation, escalated and a verified terminal refused record failed ones with the envelope retained, recovery-required stays non-terminal, and a new invocation id under a terminal owner answers the same verdict with no model and no write call. Settlement is not acceptance (the 68 clarification): a settled run whose answer was refused stays settled, and a retry is a new invocation with a new workflow_id and six new run ids. On a restart, completed receipts replay without effects; an accepted effect without a confirmed receipt requires recovery, because a crash between accepting a check and recording its result does not prove the check never ran, and the SDK alone gives no exactly-once guarantee. host_evidence is the module's report of the host's observations: one final observation per run for which a persisted answer exists, in workflow and attempt order, no run id twice, which JSON Schema cannot state and host and module both check; principal_id and observed_at are copied from that answer; null means no answer exists. It is not independent evidence: the host checks run, step and attempt membership, completeness, principal, timestamp, state and result against its durable records, and runtime slot states (absent, accepted, a refused read) belong in the host's snapshot, never here. Old runs (the embedded repair-role:<role> receipts and the request-68 explorer run) stay readable under their original formats and pins and are not decoded by this schema. No $schema keyword: the host compiles every bundle schema as draft 2020-12 and this file must carry no URL.

result.description: On completed and escalated, the record of what ran; otherwise null.

violations.description: Why the answer is not completed; empty on completed.

step.description: The role step the run served: explore, implement, review or audit.

attempt.description: The attempt index for implement and review; null for explore and audit.

run_id.description: A run of the invocation's attempt map, each at most once in the array.

principal_id.description: Copied from the run's persisted answer.

observed_at.description: RFC 3339, copied from the run's persisted answer as the host serialises its time.

role_state.description: The two states under which a persisted answer exists; a run at absent, accepted or refused has no entry.

result.description: What ran: the exploration, every attempt in order, and the integration, audit and closure where reached. Each role answer is the stored one, valid against its result schema, typed loosely here so that this schema restates none of them.

attempts.description: Attempt i at index i; an attempt that stopped before a step carries null for it.

diff_sha256.description: Over the diff's UTF-8 bytes; the diff itself stays in the host's record.

integration.description: The projection of the integrate step's thirteen-field receipt: commit, reference and tree; the whole receipt reaches the auditor in schemas/audit-request.v1.json and stays in the host's record.

closure.description: The close step's answer: one logical operation over several codec operations, assembled from pages when it did not fit inline.

before.description: The codec revision read, not a state name.

after.description: The codec revision written, not a state name.

reconciled.description: True only when the post-image, the codec receipts, the host's journal and the integration commit agree.

stopped_at.description: On escalated, the step id the workflow stopped at: close only on a known closure precondition conflict, an unknown or in-flight closure being recovery-required instead; null on completed.
